source.title: Learning Compact Neural Networks with Regularization

record.tranche_reason: Reports gradient-training outcomes in synthetic shallow-network regression experiments, using training loss rather than classification error; none of the listed versions is directly tested.
record.gate_note: The paper's experiments use synthetic regression, not CIFAR classification. Figure 2 reports training-loss curves for random initialization, but the text gives no exact values; cited results from other work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study examines regularization and initialization in synthetic shallow-network regression. It does use ReLU teacher-student networks, contrary to the record, but does not vary teacher/student widths or test extra student neurons as V2 requires. Its initialization comparisons do not test activation-matched signal propagation or trainable depth in V4. No claim version is directly tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate but omits the main conditional guarantee: projected gradient descent converges linearly to the generating weights when initialized sufficiently close, with sample requirements governed by the constraint set's covering dimension. Experiments show benefits of regularization, and the authors report that random initialization can encounter local minima, motivating data-efficient initialization methods.
record.recipe_differences: Synthetic one-hidden-layer regression experiments with ReLU and sparse or convolutional constraints; not benchmark classification training.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization and regularization choice change the reported experimental outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: With good initialization, the unregularized shallow regression network perfectly fits training data across n = 100–1000 while retaining substantial test error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unregularized shallow ReLU networks can interpolate synthetic regression training data without recovering the generating function.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report local-minimum trapping with random initialization; initialization near the teacher improves recovery and generalization in their sparse and convolutional experiments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Proximity to the generating weights can improve optimization and recovery in constrained shallow teacher-student regression.

record.problems: Synthetic regression experiments do not establish benchmark classification-error outcomes. The training-loss curves include no stated uncertainty estimates, and the paper says its experiments average 20 trials without reporting error bars in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2 contains separate training-loss curves for ℓ1 and ℓ0 regularization under random initialization, but the supplied text gives no numerical or explicit textual training-loss outcomes for those curves; exact figure-only values are not reconstructed.

untested.parts: CIFAR classification training error, including corrupted labels, and its dependence on model size, stopping time, and regularized recipes.
Changes in spurious-minimum frequency as teacher and student widths grow, and the benefit of adding one or two student neurons. Experiments use a fixed equal width of 20.
Depth degradation, identity shortcuts, and training very deep networks with special initialization or without normalization.
Activation-matched initialization, preservation of signals and gradients across layers, training speed and trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Training above an initial stability threshold, curvature adaptation, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence relative to that threshold.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Local-minimum observations at a fixed width do not establish V2's width dependence or extra-neuron remedy. Good-versus-random initialization does not establish V4's signal-propagation mechanism.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, corrupted or random labels, model size, and training duration.
The paper cites Safran and Shamir on spurious minima but does not test teacher-student ReLU networks or neuron-count effects.
Plain versus residual network depth and identity shortcuts are not tested.
Activation-matched initialization, trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization are not tested.
Learning rates above a stability limit, curvature, and edge-of-stability behavior are not tested.
Batch normalization, training speed, and learning-rate tolerance are not tested.

rows.subject: Unregularized model
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent with random initialization on a synthetic sparse-weight regression task.

conditions.value: random, W0 = Z; Z entries i.i.d. N(0, h^-1)

rows.value: The model perfectly overfits the training set for all n values (stated for the unregularized model in the discussion of Figure 1).
rows.note: Regression overfitting is related to, but does not measure, training classification error. The statement explicitly describes all n values for the unregularized model; the random-initialization training-loss curve itself is figure-only.
rows.check: The explicit perfect-training-fit statement describes Figure 1: good initialization W0 = W* + Z and n = 100–1000. R1 incorrectly assigns it to random initialization and n = 200–2000 from Figure 2. Correct those conditions and restrict the locator to Section 6.1, Figure 1. The regression fit is reported, but cannot establish any listed version's effect.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
